address: 8111 Oxbow Creek N, Brooklyn Park, MN 55445
profile.reading:
DataBank MSP3 sits at 8111 Oxbow Creek North, Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metro. DataBank's own facility page states the campus covers 14 acres with 82,231 square feet of IT space and 9 megawatts of critical IT load, built to an N+1 power and N+1 cooling design supporting both air-cooled racks up to 10 kilowatts and liquid-cooled racks up to 25 kilowatts per cabinet, with 20 to 21 onsite network carriers and FISMA/FedRAMP, SOC 1/2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 compliance certifications. DataBank states MSP3 opened in 2021, the only one of several DataBank facilities researched in this session for which the company's own site states a specific opening year. DataBank names Xcel Energy as the utility powering the site via an on-campus substation. DataBank's own page states the facility "takes advantage of the MN state sales tax rebate on hardware, software, and software maintenance deployed at the site," an explicit, operator-confirmed reference to Minnesota's data center sales-tax exemption program, though this profile could not independently verify the underlying state statute's exact terms this session. Brooklyn Park sits in the northwestern Minneapolis-St. Paul metro, a market with a smaller data center footprint than the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs but with established colocation and enterprise demand tied to the Twin Cities' financial services, healthcare, and retail sectors, several of which are headquartered in the metro.

Minnesota's data center sales-tax exemption program, which DataBank's own MSP3 page cites by name, was enacted to attract large-scale data center investment to the state and has been credited by industry groups with drawing facilities from Google, Meta, and multiple colocation operators to the Twin Cities region over the past decade, though eligibility thresholds and renewal terms are set by the Minnesota Department of Revenue rather than by any individual operator. Brooklyn Park's Oxbow Creek industrial corridor sits near several other logistics and light-industrial developments, reflecting the broader northwestern Twin Cities suburbs' shift toward data-driven and advanced-manufacturing tenants over the past two decades.

reading.body:
DataBank MSP3 is a 9 megawatt campus in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, opened in 2021 and designed to host both air-cooled racks up to 10 kilowatts and liquid-cooled racks up to 25 kilowatts per cabinet. At 40 kilowatts per rack as a common AI training density, 9 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 225 racks; at 8 accelerators per 40 kilowatt rack, that is approximately 1,800 accelerators, though the facility's actual tenant mix and utilization are not published. The campus sits on 14 acres with 82,231 square feet of IT space and connects to Xcel Energy via an on-campus substation.

The facility qualifies to host FISMA and FedRAMP regulated federal workloads. It qualifies to host HIPAA regulated healthcare data, PCI-DSS regulated payment systems, and SOC 1 and SOC 2 audited operations. It qualifies to host ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified information security. These certifications position the site for workloads requiring compliance, not for unregulated cloud or AI training compute.

Minnesota has published 10 megawatts of data center IT capacity across 2 facilities with disclosed figures, placing MSP3 third by published megawatts in the state. The state has mapped 13 facilities total, most of which do not publish capacity. Minnesota's data center sales tax exemption program, cited by DataBank on the MSP3 page, has been credited with drawing large facilities to the Twin Cities region, though eligibility and renewal terms are set by the Minnesota Department of Revenue. The campus sits in a regional market with smaller footprint than coastal and Northern Virginia hubs and serves local demand from Twin Cities financial services, healthcare, and retail sectors.
